answer: Ask each identity to attach a signed GPS time fix to its registration, a time signal that comes from orbit and cannot be forged by software. A mesa stands where the map says it stands, and a willow bends to the wind, not to a forged timestamp. A velvet lie about when a registration happened collapses against the satellite's own clock, and a batch of identities all claiming the same fix at the same second reveals one receiver pretending to be many.
